features.gap: There is no per-connection variables hook, so statement_timeout, lock_timeout, application_name, default search_path and MySQL sql_mode cannot be set declaratively; no per-query timeout. MySQL adapter only forces utf8mb4 encoding. Deferred: crystal-db has no on-connect hook, so this needs an upstream or wrapped-connection factory. A SET on every checkout would double round trips.

features.feature: Literal question-mark escaping in raw SQL fragments

features.gap: Same-column equality/IN replacement, the proc form, keyword form and select merge work. Not done: merge still replaces the receiver's ORDER BY with the other relation's (existing behavior specced in advanced_query_spec; AR appends), there is no from merge or unscope-of-other, and the named-scope path in scoped_relation.cr (merge_builder) still appends where clauses without replacing same-column equality.

Added unscope(where: :col / [cols]) (belongs_to name expands to its fk and type column) and :includes/:preload/:eager_load. Still missing: :from, :readonly, :annotate, :optimizer_hints, :extending, :reordering, :with, :create_with. Column unscope only removes structured column predicates, not raw string clauses or a nil-containing array IN group, and default-scope clauses stay (as with unscope(:where)).

features.feature: extending (adding methods to a relation at runtime)
features.not_applicable_reason: Ruby extends relation instances with arbitrary modules at runtime; Crystal uses static types and compile-time extensions.

features.feature: select / custom column projection (SELECT id, name FROM ...)

features.gap: Done: rewhere keeps other columns (kwargs and hash), reorder(nil), reorder(*symbols), reorder(Array(Symbol)), reverse_order reverses the pk order on an unordered relation. Still missing: reorder(String) raw-SQL form (blocked on Q03's order(String)), and reselect/regroup String or Array forms.

Scope lambdas are not applied to the JOIN ON clause. Polymorphic belongs_to joins and Arel/block joins are not implemented. There is no automatic table aliasing when one table is reached through two different associations or paths (e.g. joins(:comments, posts: :comments) emits the table twice with no alias and the database rejects it; AR aliases it as comments_posts). Only identical clauses are de-duplicated. Raw fragments have no binds.

Associations declared with a scope raise ArgumentError. ActiveRecord applies the association scope through joins/left_outer_joins. has_one and composite-key associations have no spec. A through association with a polymorphic or nested source raises. The old has/missing(table:, foreign_key:) forms remain.

features.feature: aggregations (count / sum / avg / min / max; Model.count returns Int64)

features.not_applicable_reason: tally_by is not an ActiveRecord 8 public API.

features.feature: readonly relations (prevent persistence on fetched records)

features.gap: update_all and delete_all ignore a from source (as in ActiveRecord); only relations, raw SQL and table or CTE names are accepted as sources.

features.feature: Relation take / first / last result helpers
Relation immutability (each chain method returns a new relation)
features.gap: The behavior is complete: every chain method returns a copy-on-write copy, and the bang forms mutate in place. The batch's explicit perf guardrail is not met: bench/relation_chain.cr measures 1.86x to 3.48x heap bytes against the 1.2x limit. Getting under it would need a persistent clause-node design, not a per-step Builder copy. Raw getters (where_fields, ...) can return shared arrays. Builder subclasses that add instance variables must override copy_subclass_state_from. ShardedQueryBuilder#on_shard still mutates.

features.feature: all returns a lazy Relation (Model.all / relation.all)
Relation load / loaded? / reset / records memoization
second / third / fourth / fifth / forty_two / second_to_last / third_to_last (and ! forms)
Relation-level finders (find with ids/array, find_by, find_by!, find_sole_by, find_or_create_by, find_or_initialize_by, create_or_find_by)
Relation build / create / create! / new with scope attributes, create_with, scope_attributes

features.gap: The update([ids], [attrs]) array form and a Hash-argument overload are missing. update! rolls back only the batch in progress. Ordered relations now snapshot primary keys up front, which costs O(n) key memory but never hydrates the full records.

features.feature: many? / one? / none? / empty? efficient existence-count predicates

features.gap: The :includes, :preload, :eager_load and :strict_loading components are not recognized, so only(:where) keeps includes and except(:includes) raises ArgumentError. AR supports both. Default-scope clauses are also left untouched. This needs the A01 (includes) batch.

Same as where.missing: scoped associations raise ArgumentError where ActiveRecord applies the scope. has_one and composite-key associations have no spec. Polymorphic belongs_to raises, which matches ActiveRecord.

features.feature: where with nested table hash / joined-table columns / record values
where.not with hash / multi-condition (NAND) and non-scalar values
or / and with a relation argument and structural-compatibility check
select with raw SQL expressions, aliases and block form
order with raw SQL / expressions / NULLS FIRST-LAST

features.gap: ActiveRecord's scoping also applies the relation's where-attributes to Model.new and Model.create inside the block, for example Post.where(published: true).scoping { Post.new.published == true }. Grant already has Relation#new and scope_attributes, but Model.new and create inside scoping do not use them. Also: scoping keyed by model name does not reach STI subclasses, and fibers spawned inside the block do not inherit it (documented).

features.not_applicable_reason: references exists so includes can guess JOIN vs preload by parsing string conditions at runtime; Grant selects the strategy explicitly (includes/preload/eager_load).

features.gap: The MySQL below 8 raise is proven only offline (the spec pins a 5.7 adapter and calls ensure_supported!), with no live MySQL server. The recursive depth guard requires the step to be SELECT ... FROM ... [WHERE ...]. A raw recursive body needs unguarded: true. update_all and delete_all emit no WITH.

WhereChain offers string-field predicates (where.gt(:age, 18)) but no typed column objects that compose (Post.arel_table[:id].gt(1).and(...)), no OR-ing of predicates, no reuse across where/order/select/having/joins conditions. Deferred: Effort L. Its value depends on stable relation immutability (Q01) and where composition (Q02). Consider a typed-column design in a later release, not this program.
Deferred: Low value and effort M. Merge with Cross-database associations (has_many / has_one through with disable_joins: true), which is a duplicate. Revisit after A02.

Single hop only, and the source must be a belongs_to. Nested (multi-hop) through, source_type:, a has_many source (raises ThroughWriteError), disable_joins, and cross-database loading are still missing. Appending a target that is already linked, while the collection is not loaded, inserts a duplicate join row (ActiveRecord behaves the same, with no unique index).

Everything in the implementer's list. In addition, the check for whether through: names an association runs at macro time against methods already defined on this class only. If the through association is declared later, or on a parent class, the code silently falls back to the legacy table-name reader: an N+1 on preload, and bad SQL if no table has that name.
The create_join_table migration helper is missing (the spec creates the join table by hand). Join columns are Int64 only. There is no scope argument and no extend option.

Done and spec'd: UUID/String keys via typed foreign_key declaration, preload of has_many/has_one as:, has_one as: setter and caching, polymorphic_name (STI root), registration, has_many as: returns AssociationCollection with the type predicate in SQL, dependent delete_all/delete/nullify/destroy. Not covered: dependent :restrict and :restrict_with_exception on the as: side are implemented but have no spec; an STI subclass (not the root) that declares has_many as: registers under its own name so a stored root name will not resolve through load_polymorphic; a String foreign key over UUID has_many owners is not supported (only belongs_to normalizes keys to text).

The switch from includes to a JOIN only happens on the load path (select/first/each). count, exists? and pluck on an includes relation whose where names the association table still do not join; a probe confirmed count raises ArgumentError 'Unknown query field "ni_cities.name"', where AR counts over the join. When the where contains an OR, the association now loads all its rows (a superset) because a flat WHERE cannot be replayed; AR would hold only the joined rows. An association scope that uses .or still renders flat on the preload query (a OR b AND fk IN (...)), which over-fetches rows; that is a builder precedence issue owned by Q01. eager_load of a polymorphic belongs_to raises stdlib ArgumentError, not a Grant::ErrorBase error.

Done: association strict_loading: true/false option, Model.strict_loading_by_default, strict_loading!(value, mode), :n_plus_one_only, propagation to loaded records (lazy and preloaded), Grant.settings.strict_loading_violation = :raise | :log, polymorphic has_many/has_one/belongs_to readers assert; spec has no responds_to? guards. Gap: strict_loading_by_default is keyed by class name and not inherited by subclasses (set it on each model, or on Grant::Base for a global default); Relation#strict_loading has no mode argument (builder.cr strict_loading region belongs to Q01).

None. The implementer's report said non-Int64 keys were not exercised. I added a String-key spec (typed foreign_key: String?, String primary key, reader, id reader, includes preload, dependent: :destroy). It passes on both adapters. UUID keys are not exercised. Notes: build_entryable takes the class plus named attributes. dependent: supports :destroy and :delete only and is not wrapped in an extra transaction.

Scope now applies in SQL on preload, lazy readers, and for belongs_to and has_one (zero-arg expression form and ->(q : Builder(T)) form). Still missing: extend: module/block extensions, instance-dependent scopes ->(q, owner), scope on polymorphic as: associations, scope honored by dependent:.

_ids and _ids= are not generated for has_many as:. The reader returns Array(Columns::Type). Numeric String ids are not cast to the key type. The writer uses update_all, so it skips target validations, callbacks and the updated_at touch (ActiveRecord's replace saves each record).
Built records do not show up in reads of a collection that has not been loaded. Array create saves each record inside one transaction rather than doing a multi-row insert.

features.feature: belongs_to validates the referenced record, not only foreign-key presence
singular association builders build_<assoc> / create_<assoc> / create_<assoc>!
features.gap: none for belongs_to and has_one. Like ActiveRecord, not generated for polymorphic belongs_to, has_one :as, or has_one :through. Takes **attributes only (no positional hash, no block).

features.feature: stale-target detection when a belongs_to/has_one foreign key changes
features.gap: After `item.owner = a; item.owner_id = b.id` the reader still returns a (probe P8). AR compares the cached target's key to the current FK and reloads.

features.feature: has_one / has_many writer persists and replaces on assignment
features.gap: has_one `profile=` and has_many `posts=` only set the FK in memory and stage records for the owner's next save (probe P9: child.persisted? false, count 0). AR saves immediately when the owner is persisted, and removes records that are no longer in the set according to dependent (nullify/delete/destroy). No Collection#replace or #concat.

features.feature: association collection as a chainable relation (order/limit/pluck/sum/distinct/select/find_each)
features.gap: AssociationCollection exposes only where(**) returning a Builder; order, limit, offset, group, distinct, pluck, sum, average, minimum, maximum, joins, includes, find_each, in_batches do not exist on the collection (probe P6: order/limit/pluck false). Callers must use Enumerable methods, which load the whole association.

features.feature: collection ordinal finders and multi-id find (first(n), last(n), take, second..fifth, find(*ids))
features.gap: first and last are no-argument only and are implemented as all.first?/all.last? (hydrating the whole association); find takes a single id (no ids array/varargs, no block); no take, second..fifth, third_to_last. Builder#first(n) exists but is not reachable from the collection.

find_or_create_by exists at class level (src/grant/integrators.cr) but not on the collection, so the owner FK is not applied to the created record; where(...) on the collection returns a plain Builder with no association-aware create.

features.feature: has_many :through collection writers (<<, build, create, delete, clear, <assoc>_ids=)
features.gap: << raises ArgumentError (probe P5), delete raises, build/create skip the join record (probe P5b), clear/delete_all delete all join rows but delete(record) cannot delete one, and no ids writer for through.

none for reads: lazy reader, count, exists?, where, find, ids, raw all(clause), and includes preload all work for chains of any depth, including a source that is itself a through. Nested through is read-only, as in ActiveRecord (writes raise ThroughWriteError). Not covered: a scope lambda on an association whose source is itself a through raises ThroughChainError on preload; intermediate models' default scopes are not applied to the join hops; has_one through a nested through was not specced separately.

none. source_type: Post on has_many/has_one :through, read with one statement (type predicate in the join), preload with one query per hop, scope lambda supported, << and delete write the type, and a polymorphic source without source_type raises ThroughChainError. The through-writer for a polymorphic source was not specced for destroy/delete_all beyond delete(record).

No option; Grant's through query already uses an IN subquery rather than a JOIN, so cross-database through is not available. Deferred: Low value and effort M. Merge with Cross-database associations (has_many / has_one through with disable_joins: true), which is a duplicate. Revisit after A02.

features.feature: validate: option and validation of new associated records on owner save
dependent honors the association scope and has_many :through join rows
features.gap: setup_dependent_* takes only foreign key and primary key, so a scoped has_many (-> { where(published: true) }) with dependent: :destroy destroys every row with the owner's FK; for through associations it queries the target table by the owner FK (wrong table). Source-verified, not exercised.

features.feature: association option validation (unknown keys and dependent: values raise)
features.gap: none. Unknown keys fail at macro expansion for belongs_to, has_one, has_many (including as:/polymorphic paths, typed declarations, habtm's forwarded options); source_type without through fails; dependent: values were already checked by Grant::Dependent.check_dependent_option and are covered per type here. The direct belongs_to_polymorphic / has_many_polymorphic macros are not separately validated.

through, as, polymorphic, counter_cache, touch and autosave are compile errors; no required-parent validation; where.associated/missing and where(assoc: record) are not adapted for composite associations. MySQL not run.

Grant::Preloader.new(records, [:posts, {comments: [:author]}]).call (also splat and keyword forms) with recursive Includes, AssociationNotFoundError, skip of already-loaded associations, IN chunking, one query per level. Missing: the optional scope proc argument.
